title: Protocol to analyze the transmigration efficiency of T. brucei using an in vitro model of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier
protocol: Determine cell density of trypanosome culture with a counting chamber.
Harvest trypanosomes by centrifugation for 10 minutes at 1,500 × g and 4°C.
Resuspend cells in pre-warmed HMI-9 medium to a final concentration of 1e7 cells/mL.
Identify filters that have reached a TEER of >600 Ω.
Empty the inserts and place them into 1 mL pre-warmed HMI-9 medium in a new 24 well plate.
Add 500 μL trypanosome suspension (i.e., 5e6 trypanosomes/filter) into the HIBCPP filter inserts.
Set up all experiments in biological duplicates.
Do not add more than 500 μL medium to the upper reservoir.
Apply only 450 μL if necessary to prevent medium from passing along the outside of the filter into the lower chamber due to capillary action.
If desired, add chemical substances to the upper reservoir for testing their influence on transmigration.
Incubate filter inserts at 37°C in a water-saturated atmosphere and 5% CO2 for 2 hours for single time point measurements.
Prepare additional wells containing 1 mL HMI-9 for kinetic experiments before each time interval.
After each time interval, transfer the HIBCPP filter insert into the next well of the prepared 24-well plate.
Carefully remove and discard the filter inserts after incubation for single time point measurements.
Resuspend transmigrated trypanosomes in each well and transfer 500 μL to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Repeat steps for resuspending and transferring samples for kinetic experiments at each interval.
Handle plates with HIBCPP filter inserts carefully to prevent spilling.
Perform gDNA isolation immediately or flash-freeze samples at -80°C.
Dilute trypanosomes from steps 1b to concentrations of 1e6, 1e5 and 1e4 cells / mL (2 mL each).
Use 500 μL of the diluted trypanosome standards for gDNA isolation.
Pipette 50 μL proteinase K into the bottom of a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 500 μL sample to the microcentrifuge tube containing proteinase K.
Add 500 μL Buffer AL to the sample and mix by pulse-vortexing for 15 s.
Incubate at 56°C for 10 min.
Briefly centrifuge the 2 mL microcentrifuge tube to remove drops from the inside of the lid.
Add 500 μL ethanol (96%–100%) to the sample and mix again by pulse-vortexing for 15 s.
After mixing, briefly centrifuge to remove drops from the inside of the lid.
Carefully apply half of the lysate to the spin column (in a 2 mL collection tube) without wetting the rim.
Close the cap and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min.
Discard the filtrate and repeat the step with the remaining lysate.
Place the spin column in a clean 2 mL collection tube.
Carefully open the spin column and add 500 μL Buffer AW1 without wetting the rim.
Close the cap and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min.
Place the spin column in a clean 2 mL collection tube and discard the old collection tube containing the filtrate.
Carefully open the spin column and add 500 μL Buffer AW2 without wetting the rim.
Close the cap and centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min.
Place the spin column in a new 2 mL collection tube and discard the old collection tube containing the filtrate.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 1 min.
Place the spin column in a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and discard the old collection tube containing the filtrate.
Carefully open the spin column and add 200 μL Buffer AE or distilled water.
Incubate at room temperature (15°C–25°C) for 1 min, and then centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min.
Prepare qPCR master mix for all samples, standards, and negative probes.
Dispense 18 μL of the master mix into each well of a 96-well qPCR plate.
Add 2 μL template DNA to each well.
Seal the qPCR plate.
Remove air bubbles by centrifuging the sealed plate.
